column10: rationale

column3: Visual organisation of concurrent terminal and agent work with durable placement and grouping.
column10: Turn keeps the navigable tree and one selected WorkSurface authoritative instead of adopting a spatial topology authority.

column3: Selection opens the exact terminal, agent, resource or project content without duplicating its runtime.
column10: The source keeps several live node surfaces on a spatial canvas; Turn adapts their distinct content into one canonical selected ViewTarget and WorkSurface while preserving each runtime.

column3: Terminal processes remain attached to durable sessions across view unmount and application restart.
column10: Warm process continuity is essential for unattended agentic work.

column3: Saved work recovers after UI restart, daemon restart, disconnect and host reboot with truthful continuity labels.
column10: Recovery is retained while Turn distinguishes reattachment from cold reconstruction.

column3: Shells, TUIs, services and logs retain complete terminal behavior alongside agent-aware processes.
column10: Generic terminal work is a first-class workload rather than an agent fallback.

column3: Agent nodes expose status, transcript, task, children, context, result and safe controls.
column10: Semantic agent information is retained in a unique WorkSurface.

column3: Groups form a recursively nestable, cycle-free hierarchy with stable order and explicit reparent semantics.
column10: The source implements recursive same-parent grouping, reparenting and cycle guards; Turn adopts that organisation while keeping Group presentation separate from runtime and CheckoutScope ownership.

column3: A group can bind its descendants to an exact repository worktree without changing runtime ancestry.
column10: Turn models this as a typed CheckoutScopeBinding on a Session group and never lets it occupy primary main.

column3: A bounded note resource can be reviewed and linked as explicit agent context.
column10: Useful operator-authored briefs are preserved without turning content into authority.

column3: Files open in a first-class editor with revision-aware atomic save and conflict recovery.
column10: Editing remains bound to the exact file backend, root and target.

column3: Repository changes and diffs are inspectable without starting or mutating a runtime.
column10: Diff inspection belongs to the selected repository scope.

column3: Static web previews, interactive browsing and video are distinct isolated resource capabilities.
column10: The source exposes separate web, browser and video node kinds; Turn adopts the distinction as non-substitutable WebPreview, Browser and Media capabilities with explicit isolation and lifecycle.

column3: Dropped or pasted media becomes a bounded inert resource rather than executable workspace input.
column10: The source bounds and exclusive-creates pasted or dropped image bytes only; Turn adapts this to MIME-declared image or video MediaImport with sealed hash, recovery saga, decoder isolation and no executable authority.

column3: Toolbar, palette and context actions share one searchable creation and command catalogue.
column10: The source palette executes renderer callbacks; Turn retains its searchable interaction but replaces callback authority with one revisioned typed CommandCatalogue shared by toolbar, palette, menus and shortcuts.

column3: Creation, navigation, close, search, panels and settings expose discoverable keyboard paths.
column10: Keyboard completeness is required for high-volume operation and accessibility.

column3: Reversible presentation mutations have deterministic undo and redo semantics under revisioned state.
column10: The source records whole-canvas presentation snapshots; Turn narrows this to eight presentation-only operations, including constant-size expand-all, with exact inverses and structurally excludes runtime, provider, SCM and authority effects.

column3: Workspace organisation, selection and recoverable resources persist without implicitly launching work.
column10: Saved presentation is data; restoration never fabricates runtime authority.

column3: First run can create a new workspace or open an existing local directory with bounded preflight.
column10: The onboarding path is brought into the shared catalogue and receipt model.

column3: A repository can be cloned into a reviewed destination with idempotent progress and partial-failure recovery.
column10: Clone is treated as an explicit operation rather than an opaque setup side effect.

column3: An SSH target can be adopted as a workspace after identity, root, capability and credential preflight.
column10: Remote onboarding never falls back to a same-named local path.

column3: Repository publication is an explicit previewed operation with remote, branch and credential receipts.
column10: Publish stays separate from create and is never automatic or remotely delegated.

column3: Captured task or output may propose a bounded safe alias while manual names always win.
column10: Turn separates local presentation aliases from provider conversation identity and title mutation.

column3: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Grok have dedicated versioned adapter identities.
column10: The complete measured roster enters one capability matrix instead of provider branches in core or UI.

column3: Operator-declared agents use the generic adapter contract and cannot acquire unproved semantics.
column10: Custom commands remain useful while unsupported capabilities stay explicit.

column3: Agent availability, version, launch modes and integration mechanisms are discovered and degrade independently.
column10: The source mainly uses static capability membership lists plus a few CLI-specific version probes; Turn adapts this into per-adapter, version, target and mechanism capability evidence with independent degradation.

column3: Provider-specific hook dialects reduce into one versioned lifecycle and topology observation contract.
column10: Structured observations are retained without leaking provider branches beyond adapters.

column3: Working, waiting, blocked, done and interrupted evidence survives reconnect and resolves deterministically.
column10: Turn keeps process lifecycle and turn state separate while routing both consistently.

column3: Subagents are discovered as stable recursive children with causal parent and attempt identity.
column10: The source discovers Claude subagents from transcript tails; Turn adapts provider-specific observations from every dedicated adapter plus OS inference into stable recursive topology with causal parent and attempt provenance.

column3: A subagent exposes bounded transcript, timing, task and result even when it owns no PTY.
column10: The source renders provider-specific subagent cards; Turn generalises them to provider-neutral canonical child nodes with bounded live activity and typed result even without a PTY.

column3: Per-conversation context use is shown with known units, window and freshness rather than guessed percentages.
column10: Context consumption remains distinct from billing quota.

column3: Account usage connectors cover Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Grok, Kimi and MiniMax with independent scope and failure.
column10: Kimi and MiniMax are required quota-only connectors; each dedicated adapter reports quota only when proved and otherwise exposes explicit unsupported state rather than a false value.

column3: Several isolated authenticated provider profiles can coexist and launch exact frozen account bindings.
column10: The source isolates several Claude homes and accounts; Turn generalises that behavior to provider-neutral AccountProfiles with exact target and profile binding and no cross-profile leakage.

column3: Requested and effective model, approval mode, flags, cwd, target and worktree are visible per attempt.
column10: The source persists requested model, account, cwd, worktree and flags but does not prove effective or current values; Turn adds requested, effective and current per-attempt receipts with provenance.

column3: A scoped model endpoint can route supported agents through an operator-owned credential reference and explicit model mapping.
column10: Gateway health, endpoint identity, TLS and effective launch receipt are modeled as a separate capability.

column3: Provider history can be discovered and paged as metadata by exact profile and target without reading bodies, implicit launch or adoption.
column10: The frozen source has a real metadata-only scan phase: scanTranscripts inventories Claude files as session id, path and modification time across local roots before any body read, but exposes neither a profile-bound nor paginated inventory. Turn adapts only that discovery facet into an exact provider, AccountProfile and ExecutionTarget ConversationInventory; body indexing remains the separate CAP-110 capability.

column3: A saved provider conversation may resume through a capability-gated native operation with continuity evidence.
column10: Resume is distinct from restart, attach and portable handoff.

column3: A supported conversation can branch while preserving source and new lineage identities.
column10: Turn labels provider branch, continuation and portable derivation separately.

column3: One agent can pull bounded transcript context from another through an explicit revocable grant.
column10: Cross-agent context transfer never implies control or ancestry.

column3: A reviewed digest and exact recent tail can move work between different agent adapters with a delivery receipt.
column10: Portable handoff is budgeted, preserves digest/tail/omission evidence and does not claim native continuity.

column3: Agents can exchange bounded typed messages through queues with durable state and independent delivery receipts.
column10: The source has bounded PTY messaging and explicitly in-memory deliver-on-idle queues with no restart catch-up; Turn adapts them to bounded typed queues with durable metadata/evidence, explicit body-loss outcomes and no synchronous join or hidden control.

column3: An operator or bounded flow can create several role-labelled agents and retain each independent result.
column10: The source spawns a presentation-level role-labelled team; Turn adapts it into an immutable versioned FlowRun that preserves every independent result and gates synthesis or judging.

column3: Provider-native loops, schedules and background jobs have stable identity, iterations and independent controls.
column10: Native job truth remains distinct from Turn Flow recurrence.

column3: An agent may create and organise bounded resources through typed capability endpoints with durable receipts.
column10: The source exposes broad direct canvas-control verbs; Turn adapts them into the exact current-agent DelegationGrant allowlist for bounded creation, organisation, context and messaging, with durable receipts, no self-expansion and no prose-derived authority.

column3: Conversation title reading and provider rename are separately discovered, fenced and receipted.
column10: Either operation may degrade without inventing the other.

column3: Operator interruption is ordered from actionable evidence rather than visual placement or terminal output polling.
column10: Turn elevates this behavior into the sole routing authority across every surface.

column3: Agent running, input-required and completed states produce consistent badges, unread state and timing.
column10: The source renderer state owns lifecycle presentation, unread state and timing; Turn adopts those facts as telemetry while typed demands remain the sole Attention authority.

column3: A permission can be answered against its exact interaction revision and remains pending until provider evidence closes it.
column10: The source uses Claude-specific local allow or deny files and optimistically flips status before provider confirmation; Turn adapts this to provider-neutral exact interaction claims, reconciliation, remote single-use grants and pending state until provider evidence.

column3: Actionable changes can notify the operator outside the window without resolving or acknowledging them.
column10: Notifications route back through the same canonical Attention target.

column3: A compact desktop projection shows urgent agent state and routes to the canonical demand.
column10: The source HUD maintains its own focus and dismissal accumulator; Turn retains the compact projection but removes its state authority so it reads and routes only canonical Attention entries.

column3: Background and headless processes can send deduplicated privacy-bounded Attention push envelopes.
column10: The source proves background delivery from actionable and completion edges; Turn adopts delivery as a privacy-bounded projection of canonical Attention while keeping acceptance, delivery, reading and demand resolution separate.

column3: Device notification grants are scope-bound, expiring, revocable and resilient to dead tokens and offline clients.
column10: The source proves device-scoped grant loading and dead-token recovery; Turn adopts that lifecycle and adds exact workspace, demand-kind, privacy, expiry and rate scope.

column3: A companion can project account usage and a bounded recent activity inbox with truthful coverage.
column10: The source mirror carries per-account usage and a bounded per-node activity inbox; Turn adopts the companion projection with exact profile, target, coverage and freshness.

column3: A headless host observes local hooks and sends outbound notifications without opening an inbound control port.
column10: Loopback observation and outbound-only delivery preserve the zero-listener deployment boundary.

column3: Automatic focus defers during typing, alternate-screen input, modal work and voice review without dropping the demand.
column10: The source provides explicit click-to-focus routes from pings and the HUD; Turn adapts them to optional automatic navigation governed by user-active-state deferral while preserving the original demand.

column3: On-device speech capture and inference run outside the control plane and never use a cloud fallback.
column10: The source offers local Whisper inside the application process alongside a cloud engine; Turn retains on-device capture but isolates inference in a least-privilege worker and forbids cloud fallback.

column3: Transcription produces an editable memory-only draft that is inserted or sent only by the foreground operator.
column10: The source inserts transcription directly into the selected terminal after recording ends without submitting Enter; Turn adapts this to a frozen-target editable memory-only draft and explicit Insert or Send.

column3: Speech models have explicit install, digest, size, licence, offline-use and deletion lifecycle.
column10: The source provides explicit local model download, inventory, deletion and offline use; Turn adopts that lifecycle and adds exact digest, size, licence and provenance verification.

column3: A self-hosted browser surface uses the same hierarchy, terminal, repository and Attention protocols.
column10: The full surface preserves revisions and recovery while withholding desktop-only authority.

column3: Remote runtimes, files and repositories remain bound to an authenticated host generation and exact root.
column10: No remote outage may produce a same-name local effect.

column3: Companion pairing establishes revocable end-to-end encrypted device identity with replay protection.
column10: The source combines pairing with relay and SSH device powers plus separate E2EE primitives; Turn adapts this to exact Invitation, Client and Session identities, one-use bootstrap and replay fences, scoped roles and atomic revocation.

column3: Collaborators can expose bounded presence and selection without granting input or control authority.
column10: The source presence hub is bounded, ephemeral and non-authoritative; when shared remotely its confidentiality comes from the separately authenticated encrypted sharing transport.

column3: An authenticated full remote surface may create ordinary work, navigate views and type under an exact input lease.
column10: The source provides authenticated remote creation, navigation and terminal use; Turn adopts those operations through the common typed mutation protocol while SAF-005 supplies the exclusive input lease.

column3: Destructive lifecycle, provider deletion, external close, repository publication, secrets, trust and authority stay desktop-foreground-only.
column10: Turn deliberately keeps a stronger safety boundary while retaining ordinary remote creation, viewing and input.

column3: Repository status supports stage, unstage, discard, branch, commit, sync and push with exact scope and consequences.
column10: Source-control operations are first-class target-bound tools.

column3: Worktree creation, reconciliation and assignment support concurrent agent-per-branch work without locking primary main.
column10: The source creates, binds, removes and merges worktrees and may merge or push through the base checkout; Turn adds isolated CheckoutScope ownership and reconciliation plus the invariant that primary main remains operator-only.

column3: Repository hosting authentication and issue operations use an explicit credential seam with isolated failures.
column10: The source has one GitHub credential and issue integration; Turn generalises it into a non-secret RepositoryHostProfile plus independently revocable RepositoryBackend and WorkItemSource grants.

column3: A board projects live Sessions, Agents and WorkItems as alternate views over their canonical identities and runtimes.
column10: Turn preserves source board behavior by projecting the same canonical Session, Agent and WorkItem identities: selection opens their existing WorkSurface/runtime, Session and Agent status is read-only where no WorkItem field applies, and board edits use only WorkItem-owned authority without creating a second identity, runtime or lifecycle authority.

column3: External issue cards retain source identity and support conflict-aware move, close and reopen reconciliation.
column10: External state is mapped through a rate-limited credential-isolated WorkItemSource.

column3: A workspace file explorer navigates and edits only the selected target and root.
column10: The source explorer follows the active workspace and remote route; Turn adopts that interaction under exact FileBackend target, root and generation paging while file open and save remain separate operations.

column3: Commit history, graph and changed files are inspectable within the exact repository boundary.
column10: History inspection is read-only until a separate typed repository operation is chosen.

column3: A configured local agent may propose a commit message from a bounded staged diff without executing repository changes.
column10: The source bounds the staged diff but launches a configurable helper in repository cwd with inherited environment; Turn retains proposal UX while removing repository, credential, environment and network authority under exact sandbox and resource limits.

column3: Host memory totals, availability, swap and pressure are reported per exact execution target with freshness and coverage.
column10: Unknown or failed collection never appears as zero and remote targets never use local data.

column3: Process-tree memory is attributed to runtime attempts and nodes while closed owners and unmatched survivors remain visible.
column10: Stable process identity, shared-runtime buckets and partial coverage prevent double counting or invented splits.

column3: Live handles unmatched to current attempts are recoverable as target-scoped inventory with exact adopt, ignore or terminate actions.
column10: The source inventories unmatched tmux sessions and supports navigation or termination; Turn adapts this to target-wide runtime handles with honest coverage and exact adopt, ignore or terminate actions.

column3: Multiple viewers can attach while one explicit revisioned lease owns input and resize.
column10: The source allows every co-attached client to write and explicitly permits concurrent writers to interleave; Turn replaces that with one revisioned input and resize lease while retaining multiple viewers.

column3: Usage, reset windows and recent account activity are projected per exact provider profile and target.
column10: The source mirror combines per-account usage windows with a bounded activity inbox; Turn adopts a profile- and target-scoped projection with independent freshness and coverage.

column3: File upload and download use reviewed target-bound tickets, confinement and bounded transfer state.
column10: The source provides capped staging uploads and shell-specific one-use downloads but no single dual-endpoint transfer contract; Turn adapts them to reviewed expiring tickets with endpoint generations, hash, chunk and expiry fences plus atomic create-new reconciliation.

column3: Application updates are discovered, staged and applied through an explicit platform-aware lifecycle.
column10: The source automatically downloads updates and installs them on application quit; Turn adapts this to separately signed manifest and package domains with explicit foreground apply, anti-rollback, reconciliation and rollback.

column3: Bounded product announcements are shown without masquerading as operational Attention.
column10: The source supplies dismissible product-banner and feed interaction; Turn adopts it while adding an independent signed announcement domain, inert content and reviewed links separate from StatusEvent and Attention.

column3: Decorative mascot, pet and game representation beyond canonical operational state and Attention.
column10: Turn excludes only redundant mascot, pet and game presentation; source mascot and brand-pulse animation may reflect working or done as a supporting projection, while canonical operational state and Attention remain owned by CAP-046, CAP-049 and CAP-093.

column3: The active terminal or text surface supports bounded find navigation without consuming terminal input.
column10: The source provides forward, backward and wrapping search over a terminal and transcript snapshot without terminal input; Turn adopts the interaction and adds exact source revision, scan and match budgets.

column3: Terminal, note and editor content can switch to a sanitised markdown projection without changing source data.
column10: The source supplies a DOM-sanitised Markdown projection without mutating source content; Turn adopts it while pinning source revision, blocking network and local-image fetches and opening links only through a separate reviewed Browser operation.

column3: Board mutations and comments expose an ordered activity history tied to canonical work identities.
column10: The source supplies an append-only bounded BoardLog of comments and events; Turn adopts that history as a canonical WorkItem provenance stream with deterministic revisions, pagination and echo deduplication.

column3: Terminal font, theme, contrast, zoom and preview settings preserve readable keyboard-operable output.
column10: Appearance controls are retained within the accessibility contract and cannot obscure semantic status.

column3: Top-level work in the active work surface can be compacted into a non-overlapping grid through one layout action.
column10: Turn continuously derives the canonical tree row layout, eliminating a cleanup action while preserving logical order and avoiding a second spatial authority.

column3: Commercial licence activation, subscription upgrade, paid-seat enforcement and entitlement gating.
column10: Turn excludes monetisation and entitlement gates because they do not contribute to operator control; they cannot affect feature availability, authority or telemetry.

column3: A bounded local diagnostic log can be viewed, filtered, copied and explicitly cleared.
column10: Turn retains operator-visible diagnostics while adding structured redaction, explicit coverage/freshness and durable deletion fences to the existing bounded buffer and clear action.

column3: Settings are grouped, searchable, directly addressable and resettable by section.
column10: Turn adapts the single settings surface to the Global, Workspace, Template, Session and Temporary hierarchy with stable deep links, effective-source labels and revision-fenced per-section reset.

column3: Operator-visible diagnostics can seed an editable bug-report draft whose external issue link is opened only after review.
column10: Turn retains report preparation as a capability independent from log viewing, while adding an exact inclusion/redaction manifest and a separate foreground export or link-open action.

column3: Collaborators can exchange short cursor-scoped ephemeral text without creating durable context, Attention, input or control authority.
column10: Turn keeps fast co-presence chat distinct from agent messaging and durable handoff, while adding exact scope/revision, expiry, redaction, rate and retract semantics with no operational authority.

column3: Local or remote images and PDF documents open in a revision-pinned view with page, zoom, search and print controls.
column10: Turn separates non-text document viewing from the editor and Media playback, using bounded revocable blobs, isolated decoding and exact source revisions without granting content authority.

column3: Terminal copy, paste and path drop reach the local clipboard or PTY only through bounded operator gestures; terminal-controlled clipboard escape sequences are denied.
column10: The source accepts write-only terminal clipboard escape payloads; Turn adapts copy/paste/drop into typed gesture-bound operations and denies both clipboard read and write escape directions.

column3: Optional configurable sound cues distinguish completed turns from work that needs the operator.
column10: Distinct non-blocking cues improve high-volume attention routing while remaining optional, rate-limited and supplementary to accessible visual state.

column3: A resumable guided tour discovers capabilities and leads provider authentication, consent and remote-trust setup without blocking terminal work.
column10: Turn retains progressive setup while binding every authentication, notification, microphone and remote-trust step to explicit capability discovery, consent and recoverable skip/cancel semantics.

column3: One reviewed operation can restart and resume a bounded set of eligible idle agents while excluding active, blocked, background or unresumable work.
column10: Turn preserves high-volume recovery ergonomics but adds a revision-pinned candidate preview, per-instance sequential receipts, idempotent retry and an exact skipped/failed/restarted summary.

column3: An agent can navigate and interact with only the isolated Browser nodes it created under a reviewed Workspace capability.
column10: Turn preserves bounded agent-driven browser work while replacing inherited repository flags with explicit local adoption, exact instance/attempt ownership, typed receipts and visible stop/revoke controls.

column3: Eligible idle off-screen agent runtimes can hibernate and later resume automatically under an opt-in conservative policy.
column10: Turn adapts automatic resource saving to exact activity and resumability evidence, excludes any runtime with uncertain or live work, preserves durable continuity and wakes without an operator interaction or Attention loss.

column3: Anonymous product install-count and event telemetry sent to a product-operated endpoint.
column10: Turn rejects product telemetry, stable analytics identifiers and install-count reporting; narrowly purpose-bound update checks may fetch signed update metadata without identity, analytics payload or cross-purpose reuse.

column3: A Companion-started terminal or agent session can consume host launch settings and register a bounded Node in an existing project.
column10: The frozen source proves only host launch-setting publication and registration of an already-started session; the Companion-side launch effect lives outside this snapshot. Turn adapts that handoff to a reviewed grant/template, preassigned identities and one idempotent receipt without claiming source evidence of launch.

column3: Unreadable workspace/project state is quarantined byte-for-byte before an empty/default state can be loaded or saved.
column10: Turn preserves the source's corrupt-file sidelining but requires exact hash-addressed quarantine, crash-safe no-overwrite ordering and one honest recovery route; corrupt data is never silently presented as a successful empty load or deleted.

column3: Repositories expose typed branch, history-rewrite, stash, revert, merge and initialization operations without raw Git arguments.
column10: Turn preserves the advanced source-control verbs but adds exact repository/ref revisions, non-primary-worktree containment, consequence review for destructive or rewriting actions and durable subphase reconciliation instead of direct raw command dispatch.

column3: Externally observed workspace/project changes are surfaced and reconciled without silently overwriting dirty local presentation state.
column10: Turn replaces parallel filesystem authority over its internal store with daemon single-writer revisioned StateStream mutations; authenticated peer changes merge additively, self-echoes deduplicate and hostile filesystem edits quarantine rather than erase live Sessions or runtimes.

column3: Eligible hidden Browser renderers can be visibly discarded and automatically rehydrated without losing canonical Node identity or bypassing navigation policy.
column10: Turn preserves the source's opt-in five-minute hidden-renderer reclamation and loading, audible and agent-control exclusions, while adding exact revision/safety suppressors, visible loss truth, reviewed public-navigation revalidation, idempotent automatic rehydration and bounded crash/resource proof without ambient credentials or implicit localhost/local-file access.

column3: Operators may hide selected non-critical controls without hiding safety, recovery or keyboard-operable palette access.
column10: Turn preserves the source's closed hideable-control inventory and fail-visible unknown ids, while requiring Attention, recovery, destructive and Delete/Restart/Search/Close controls to remain visible and every hidden action to remain in a completely keyboard-operable command palette without requiring its own global shortcut.

column3: ExecutionTarget PTY capacity is measured, warned and safely remediated before terminal creation reaches the system wall.
column10: Turn preserves the source's 80% warning and safe-headroom critical band where used is at least ceiling minus required headroom, before literal exhaustion, plus visible recovery guidance; it requires exact target/freshness truth, pre-refusal Attention, no silent process kill and a reviewed durable reconcileable rollback-capable privileged mutation—or explicit rejection of auto-elevation where that proof is unavailable.

column3: Many agent Nodes share one provider runtime endpoint while retaining stable signed per-instance thread identity and explicit fallback.
column10: Turn preserves the source's restart-stable signed Codex thread binding and explicit degradation, generalises it to provider RuntimeEndpoints and deliberately keeps provider-account scope outside this identity; absence of account metadata never becomes a CAP-032 profile claim.

column3: Off-screen terminal viewers and PTY clients may be parked without ending durable work and reattach automatically on return.
column10: Turn preserves ten-minute off-screen viewer reclamation, bounded LRU parking and zero-PTY tmux control clients only behind exact durable-work survival, watcher, input and Attention proof; plain-shell or uncertain work is protected, resource release is truthful, and selection reattaches automatically without a Start pane or respawned painter.

column3: Automatic killing of sufficiently idle detached durable sessions when detached-count, memory, swap, PSI or PTY pressure crosses a configured limit.
column10: Turn rejects the source's pressure- or cap-triggered tmux session kill policy: age and silence are eligibility inputs, not independent triggers; measurement may raise Attention and reclaim proved reconstructible viewers/clients, while ending durable work remains an exact foreground reviewed lifecycle operation or the separately explicit conservative Eco contract.

column3: Downstream agent work starts once immutable typed dependency results satisfy an idempotent readiness policy.
column10: Turn preserves source --after graph creation, persisted armed launch, visible dependency edges and automatic start, but replaces idle/done guesses, deleted-as-success and manual run-now escape with typed immutable DependencyResult evidence and a durable idempotent StepStartPolicy receipt.

column3: Private bounded full-text search spans authorised profiled conversation bodies and opens the canonical result view without resuming work.
column10: Turn adapts the source's local persisted transcript-body index to explicit opt-in, mandatory AccountProfile/target/conversation/revision scope, bounded redacted indexing and query, freshness/coverage/gap truth and deletion/rebuild proof; endpoint_unscoped body search is unsupported, and selecting a hit opens its canonical ViewTarget without resume or input.

column3: Session End/Delete completes navigation atomically while uncertain survivors move to bounded recovery inventories instead of vetoing closure.
column10: Turn replaces source surface-specific and remote-incomplete kill routing with the nonblocking container-close transaction of PRD-VIE-008 and PRD-LIF-006: exact owned effects are attempted once, uncertain live work is retained in recovery inventory, and no save or cleanup failure demands a second user action or resurrects the row.

column3: Recycle, foreground terminate, kill, restart and resume are distinct typed operations over one exact runtime attempt.
column10: Turn preserves the source's distinct recycle, subscriber detach/kill and foreground-process termination paths while binding restart/resume/terminate/kill to exact instance, attempt, runtime handle, generation, authority and idempotent receipt; none substitutes Session End/Delete or generic terminal fidelity.
